name: 105 Spadina Avenue
summary: Located at Spadina Avenue and Adelaide Street West, 105 Spadina will build culture and inclusivity in the Spadina-Fort York community by delivering a new mixed-use development.
description:
In December 2020, the CreateTO Board and City Council approved a proposed transaction with 105 Spadina Avenue's adjacent landowner that completes the disposition of a portion of the City-owned surface parking lots at 105 Spadina Avenue and 363 Adelaide Street West in order to facilitate the construction of the new development and city-building opportunity at 105 Spadina Avenue. 

The City-owned properties at 105 Spadina Avenue and 363 Adelaide Street West offers an exciting development opportunity for the Spadina-Fort York neighbourhood. Currently a 36-space surface parking lot operated by the Toronto Parking Authority (TPA), the City of Toronto, CreateTO, and the TPA have collectively explored opportunities to unlock additional value from this City-owned surface parking lot in order to construct a new 10,764 square foot public park, a new mixed-use, high-rise development and on-site below-grade public parking that will be used to generate additional funds for an estimated 25-30 affordable housing units in the area. This mixed-use development will foster community-building while maximizing the land use.

The construction of these new City-owned facilities will be entirely funded by proceeds from the transaction.

name: 1113-1117 Dundas Street West
summary: Led by CreateTO as public builder, this new mass timber rental housing development on City-owned land will deliver 74 rental homes, including affordable rental homes. The 10-storey project, in Toronto’s west end, will help create more homes for families through an innovative and sustainable City-led approach.
description:
1113-1125 Dundas Street West is a new rental housing development on City-owned land in Toronto’s Spadina-Fort York community, led by CreateTO as public builder. As the first CreateTO public builder project to break ground, the development marks an important milestone in a new City-led approach to delivering housing on public land. 
CreateTO, on behalf of the City of Toronto, is repurposing the site (formerly occupied by a Green P surface parking lot and a vacant, semi-detached home) to create 74 new rental homes, including at least 17 affordable homes. Designed to support a range of households, the development will include family-sized units in a vibrant, transit-oriented neighbourhood. 
By leveraging City-owned land and a City-led delivery model, the project demonstrates how the public sector can help create more housing, faster and efficiently, while supporting affordability and sustainability. The development reflects a collaborative effort between CreateTO and the City of Toronto to advance housing solutions that deliver lasting community benefit. 
Sustainability has been a guiding principle of the project from the outset, as part of the Mass Timber Pilot Program launched by CreateTO and City partners. It explores how innovative, low-carbon construction methods can support faster, more sustainable housing delivery, the development incorporated sustainability at every stage. 
In preparation for redevelopment, the vacant home on the site at 1113 Dundas Street West was carefully deconstructed rather than demolished, allowing materials to be diverted from landfill and supporting a more circular approach to construction. 
The new building will incorporate mass timber construction, geothermal energy and other low-carbon design strategies to reduce environmental impacts and support a more sustainable community. 
Construction is scheduled to begin in Summer 2026 and continue through 2027. 
This project is supported in part through funding provided by the Government of Canada under Build Canada Homes, supporting the development of affordable and non-market housing.
Key Project Facts
10-storey rental housing building 

74 new rental homes, including at least 17 affordable homes and family-sized units 

Mass timber construction and geothermal energy systems 

78 bicycle parking spaces 

Private resident amenity space 

Key Project Milestones
2022: CreateTO and City partners launch the Mass Timber Pilot Program. 

2023/2024: Community consultation and submission of an Official Plan and Zoning By-Law Amendment. 

2024: Planning approvals are secured for the development. 

2025: Site preparation begins, including the deconstruction of the existing vacant home. Check out a timelapse and deconstruction photos below. 

Summer 2026: Construction begins for CreateTO's first public builder project. 

Have a question about the 1113 – 1125 Dundas Street West Mass Timber Pilot project or want to sign up for project updates? If so, email masstimber@createto.ca 
Note: The address for this project is 1113-1125 Dundas Street West, but the site is commonly referred to as 1113-1117 Dundas Street West.

name: 1250 Eglinton Avenue West
summary: Located at Eglinton Avenue West and W. R. Allen Road, 1250 Eglinton Avenue West will deliver a new mixed-income, mixed-use, transit-oriented development with 240 new homes, including 80 new affordable rental units.
description:
The 1250 Eglinton Avenue West site is currently a parking lot used by Metrolinx and will be transformed to become a new mixed-income and mixed-use development with access to the new Cedarvale station on the Eglinton crosstown LRT and the existing Eglinton West TTC station. The development will include 240 new residential units, with 80 being affordable rental units. 

1250 Eglinton Avenue West is a project part of the Housing Now Initiative to invest in City-owned lands across Toronto for the development of affordable housing within mixed-income, mixed-use, transit-oriented communities.
